text: The model flagged three things that push the applicant’s default risk upward. First, the revolving‑credit utilization is about 48 % of the available limit; this alone adds a sizable positive amount (+0.34) to the risk score, meaning the model sees a relatively high balance as a warning sign. Second, the applicant holds three real‑estate or mortgage loans; each of those contributes another +0.26, reflecting the extra debt burden from property financing. Third, there are 13 open credit lines and loans, which adds +0.18, indicating many active accounts that could strain cash flow. Together, these three factors increase the calculated risk, but the overall calculation still falls on the “low‑risk” side of the model’s threshold.
